title: How do magnets work?
examples: Does a magnet work without electricity?
What is the difference between attracting and repelling?
Can you make a magnet work if I put it near wood?

explain.say: Today we say how magnets work. We will learn about their poles. Poles are the ends of a magnet. They are always marked as north and south.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: a bar magnet. Look at the north pole, the south pole and the field lines. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Magnets can push or pull things. This is called attraction or repulsion. Opposite poles always attract each other. North pulls to south.
Like poles push away from each other. This is called repulsion. North pole pushes away from another north pole. South pushes away from south.
Not all materials are magnetic. Only some materials can be pulled by magnets. Iron and steel are good examples of these materials.
Think about a refrigerator magnet. It sticks to the metal door. The magnet is attracting the metal of the fridge.
A common mistake is thinking magnets have only one pole. But every magnet has two poles. You must always have both north and south.

faq.q: Why do magnets only attract certain metals?
faq.a: Magnets are attracted to materials that have certain magnetic properties. These materials are called ferromagnetic. You might also ask, "What kind of metal do magnets stick to?" or "Are all metals magnetic?"

faq.q: Do the poles always stay the same if I move the magnet?
faq.a: Yes, the poles always remain north and south. This is a fixed property of the magnet. You could also ask, "Can I swap the poles?" or "Does moving it change the poles?"

faq.q: If I push two magnets together, why do they push apart?
faq.a: They push apart because the like poles are repelling each other. This is a fundamental rule of magnetism. You might ask, "Why do they push?" or "What happens when poles are the same?"

faq.q: Can magnets attract things that are not metal?
faq.a: Generally, magnets only attract magnetic materials like iron. They do not attract things like plastic or wood. You might ask, "Will it stick to plastic?" or "Does it work on wood?"

faq.q: What is the difference between attraction and repulsion?
faq.a: Attraction means the poles pull towards each other, like opposites. Repulsion means the poles push away from each other, like likes. You could ask, "Which way do they pull?" or "What is pushing apart?"
asks: What is the force between poles?

facts: Magnets have two poles: a North pole and a South pole.
Opposite poles attract, meaning a North pole pulls a South pole.
Like poles repel, meaning two North poles push each other away.
Magnets are strongest at their poles.

quiz.say: If you bring a North pole near a North pole, what happens?
quiz.why: Like poles always push away from each other, which is called repulsion.

wrong.0: This is wrong because only opposite poles attract each other.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the poles exert a noticeable pushing force.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the magnetic force remains strong.

quiz.say: Which of these materials is typically magnetic?
quiz.why: Steel is a type of iron alloy that is known to be strongly attracted to magnets.

wrong.1: Plastic is not a magnetic material and will not be pulled by a magnet.
wrong.2: Wood is an organic material that does not interact with magnetic fields.
wrong.3: Rubber is a polymer that lacks the necessary magnetic properties.

quiz.say: If a magnet has a North pole on the left and a South pole on the right, what will happen if you bring a second magnet with the same pole on the left?
quiz.why: When like poles meet, they always push away from each other.

wrong.0: This is wrong because the rule is that like poles repel.
wrong.1: This is wrong because the force is one of pushing, not sticking.
wrong.2: This is wrong because the magnetic force is always present.
